run.question: The payment-api pod in namespace app-100a had issues on November 21, 2026 around 13:45 UTC. What happened?

report.summary: Between about 2026-11-21T13:49:24Z and 2026-11-21T14:44Z the payment-api application in namespace app-100a (Loki stream job=payment-api, service=payment-api, pod_name=payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-55fp6) logged repeated level=ERROR entries for exhaustion of its database connection pool: 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' (error_code DB_CONN_001, stack at PaymentService.processPayment() then DatabasePool.acquire()) plus 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' reporting pool_size 20, active_connections 20 and waiting_requests 27-46 with wait_time_ms 5216-26789. In the same window the app's own /healthz check returned status_code 503 with the message 'Health check failed - database unreachable' and response times of 5009-9684 ms. Before the onset the service logged normal payments and fast DB queries (15 ms at 13:20:57Z, 65 ms at 13:34:45Z); during the episode DB queries took 1252 ms (13:50:55Z) and 2355 ms (14:43:57Z), and after recovery 20-77 ms with successful payments from 14:48:12Z. The evidence shows a self-reported database dependency failure propagating into payment-api pool saturation and failed health checks; the database is not a workload in this cluster (no database pod, Service or Endpoint exists) and its endpoint/credentials sit in Secret payment-api-100a-script, which cannot be read, so the deepest cause is unverified. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable for every attempt, so no error-rate, latency series, kube-state-metrics or trace evidence was obtained; a pod-log read of the current pod returned no data, and NetworkPolicy listing returned no rows.

claims.text: The payment-api log stream in app-100a repeatedly logged 'ConnectionPoolExhausted: All connections in use' (error_code DB_CONN_001, stack at PaymentService.processPayment() then DatabasePool.acquire()) and 'Failed to acquire database connection - pool exhausted' with pool_size 20, active_connections 20, waiting_requests between 27 and 46 and wait_time_ms between 5216 and 26789, from 2026-11-21T13:49:24Z through 2026-11-21T14:43:57Z.

payment-api's own health check reported 'Health check failed - database unreachable' on endpoint /healthz with status_code 503 and response_time_ms 5009 at 2026-11-21T13:57:29Z, 9684 at 14:01:50Z and 6354 at 14:44:44Z.

Before the error onset the same service logged normal operation inside the incident window: 'Payment processed successfully' with processing_time_ms 468 at 2026-11-21T13:31:51Z, a DEBUG cache hit at 13:43:12Z, and 'Database query executed' durations of 15 ms (13:20:57Z) and 65 ms (13:34:45Z).

During the error episode the same 'Database query executed' log shows elevated durations of 1252 ms at 2026-11-21T13:50:55Z and 2355 ms at 14:43:57Z, and after the errors stopped the durations were 40 ms (15:01:00Z), 20 ms (15:05:45Z), 54 ms (15:07:38Z) and 77 ms (15:14:43Z) with successful payments logged from 14:48:12Z onward; these are individual samples, not a statistical baseline comparison.

The Loki count_over_time series by level for namespace=app-100a, job=payment-api (10-minute buckets) shows the ERROR series first nonzero in the bucket ending 2026-11-21T13:49:42Z (1 line) and continuing through the bucket ending 14:54:42Z (1 line), consistent with the first observed error line 13:49:24Z and the last returned error line 14:44:44Z.

No database workload is observable in the cluster: the only pods in app-100a are loki-66445c6d6f-9qwzw and payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-55fp6, the only deployments/replicasets in app-100a are loki-66445c6d6f and payment-api-100a-64dcc58445, the cluster Service list contains no database service, and the app-100a Endpoints object set contains only the loki Service.

Deployment payment-api-100a runs container payment-api from image python:3.9-slim with command ['python','/app/app-direct-push.py'], a single downward-API env var HOSTNAME, a memory limit of 256Mi, an HTTP livenessProbe on /healthz:8080, and mounts the application code from volume app-script which is Secret payment-api-100a-script; no database host, credential or pool-size setting appears in the container env.

The cluster objects observed now postdate the incident: pod payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-55fp6 has startTime 2026-11-22T09:41:33Z and restartCount 0, and Deployment payment-api-100a reports creationTimestamp 2026-11-22T09:41:33Z, generation 1, revision 1 and replicas/available/ready 1, so their status cannot describe the incident-time pod.

The only Kubernetes Events retained in the authorized window are 14 events clustered at 2026-11-22T09:21:00Z-09:41:34Z (2 Deployment ScalingReplicaSet, 2 ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, 2 Pod Scheduled/Created/Pulled/Started, 2 Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint); no event from 2026-11-21 is present.

Node opspilot-m1-control-plane reported MemoryPressure=False (KubeletHasSufficientMemory), DiskPressure=False, PIDPressure=False and Ready=True at the time of observation, which is after the incident window.

The most likely cause of the 13:49-14:45Z failure is degradation of the external database that payment-api depends on (unreachable or very slow), which held all 20 pooled connections, queued 27-46 waiting requests for up to 26.8 s and made /healthz return 503 after 5-9.7 s; this is supported by the app's own 'database unreachable' health-check message and DB query samples of 1252 ms and 2355 ms during the episode versus 15-77 ms samples before and after, but the database itself is not in the cluster and could not be examined.

Alternative candidate that remains open: a connection leak or misconfigured pool size inside the payment-api application itself (pool_size 20 was fixed in the app configuration, which lives in the unreadable Secret payment-api-100a-script) rather than a database-side fault; the elevated DB query durations and 'database unreachable' message argue against this but do not exclude an application-level leak.

Alternative candidate that remains open: a request/load increase around 13:49Z saturated the 20-connection pool (waiting_requests 27-46 at every sampled error); this is not confirmed because no request-rate, throughput or concurrency metric was obtainable and log volume per 10-minute bucket stayed in a narrow range across the onset.

Container termination as the cause (OOMKill, eviction or crash-loop) is not supported by the returned rows: the pool-exhaustion and health-check error text describes database connection acquisition failures rather than process termination, and the log query over 2026-11-21T12:00-15:15Z for start/listen/pool/init/shutdown/restart patterns returned only these runtime error lines and no startup or shutdown line.

Nothing in the cluster objects ties the failure to a Kubernetes-side misconfiguration or to another workload: app-100a contains only the payment-api Deployment/pod and the loki Deployment/pod with its Service and Endpoints, there is no Service or Endpoints entry for payment-api, no database Service exists cluster-wide, and the node reports no memory, disk or PID pressure at observation time.

Obtain the database side of the picture for 2026-11-21T13:45-14:45Z (availability, connection count, slow queries) and read the payment-api application configuration in Secret payment-api-100a-script to learn the configured DB endpoint and pool_size, since those are what would let the deepest cause be named.

Restore the Prometheus and Jaeger read paths and re-check payment-api error-rate, latency and restart series for 13:45-15:00Z so the error rate, latency and restart behaviour can be quantified rather than inferred from logs; both sources returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE with source_contact=possible on every attempt in this Run.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable on every attempt (get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE with source_contact=possible), so no error-rate, latency-histogram, kube-state-metrics replica/restart or OOM series exist for the incident window; those signals are unknown, not zero.

Jaeger was unavailable (traces_search and traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no span-level evidence exists for any service, including whether payment-api emitted spans or which caller was affected.

The pod-log read fetch_pod_logs for payment-api-100a-64dcc58445-55fp6 returned status no_data with zero lines from both the current and previous container instances (previous instance reported not found), so container runtime history for that pod is unknown, not absent.

The database that payment-api depends on is not a Kubernetes object here: no database pod, Deployment/ReplicaSet, Service or Endpoint exists in app-100a or cluster-wide, and its address and credentials live in Secret payment-api-100a-script, which cannot be read, so its availability, latency and identity at 13:49-14:45Z could not be verified.

The exact trigger and onset are unknown: logs are sparse (1-4 lines per 10-minute bucket), the last pre-error line returned was 13:43:12Z and the first error line 13:49:24Z, so whether degradation began at 13:45Z cannot be established; the end is bracketed only between 14:44:44Z (last error line) and 14:48:12Z (first success).

No Kubernetes Event exists for 2026-11-21 in the cluster: retained events cover only 2026-11-22T09:21:00Z-09:41:34Z, so kubelet eviction, OOMKilled or liveness-probe-kill events during the incident are unverifiable; the Deployment does carry a /healthz livenessProbe with failureThreshold 3.

Whether the incident-time payment-api container restarted is unknown; the current pod was created 2026-11-22T09:41:33Z after the incident with restartCount 0, and historical restart series were unobtainable.

The cluster-wide NetworkPolicy listing returned status no_data with zero rows, so it cannot be stated whether a NetworkPolicy restricted payment-api egress to its database; that view is a limit of this Run, not proof of absence.

No fault-injecting ConfigMap or other object was found for payment-api-100a (only kube-root-ca.crt and loki-config exist in app-100a; flagd-config in otel-demo belongs to the separate otel-demo demo app), but the payment-api script is stored in an unreadable Secret, so injected or hard-coded fault settings in that script could not be checked.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no deployment or configuration change history around 2026-11-21T13:45Z could be examined.
next_steps: Check database-side telemetry for 2026-11-21T13:45-14:45Z (availability, connection saturation, slow-query latency) for the endpoint payment-api uses.
Have the owner review Secret payment-api-100a-script (app-direct-push.py) for the DB endpoint, the pool_size 20 setting, connection timeouts and any injected fault or delay logic.
Re-query Prometheus and Jaeger when reachable for payment-api error rate, request latency and container restart/OOM series in 13:45-15:00Z.
Confirm from the platform team whether the payment-api pod was restarted or rescheduled during the incident, since that pod no longer exists.
